Versand Lieferzeit Versand in 14-17 Tagen Anzahl In den Warenkorb Zur Wunschliste hinzufügen E-Mail an einen Freund Zum Ende der Bildergalerie springen Zum Anfang der Bildergalerie springen Details In memory of one of the (if not THE) last true rock’n’roll icons, OKKO presents the MOTÖRBASS pedal. You’re all familiar with Lemmy’s signature sound – ultra powered rumbling grind, distorted, slightly fuzzy but with a lot of edge and definition for high speed hammering powerchords. It would be presumptuous to claim you could get the exact sound of the iconic modified Marshall Super Bass stack from a 9-volts-powered box... but we did a lot of tweaking to capture that sonic character and we’re pretty happy with the result. When trying the recreate the Lemmy sound with distortion pedals you easily run into problems. Bass distortions often lack the aggressive edge or get muddy when playing chords. Guitar distortions usually cut too much low end and often sound too fizzy. The MOTÖRBASS runs on an internal voltage of 24 volts*. Paired with carefully chosen filtering, this massive headroom ensures for a raw but tight distortion sound all across the fretboard. Controls are easy: FASTER controls the gain from almost clean to full blast. HARDER works on the upper mids. Lower settings sound more rounded, turning up adds aggressive bite and attack. LOUDER? makes it louder

sources.excerpt: --> OKKO FX MOTÖRBASS Demo Review | Loopy Demos Show or hide the side bar navigation Loopy Demos Demos Posts Manufacturers About Contact Demos Posts Manufacturers About Contact All demos OKKO FX MOTÖRBASS Oct 4, 2023 Read next What is the Best Bass Overdrive Pedal? The MOTÖRBASS by OKKO FX is one of those pedals I honestly didn’t expect to fall for. I’ve never been a Motörhead devotee, and recreating Lemmy’s bass tone isn’t exactly on my to-do list. But what OKKO has built here goes well beyond a tribute. It’s a straightforward, punchy bass distortion that plays well in a rock mix without eating your low end alive. The way the bass functions in Motörhead is almost like a second rhythm guitar: heavily distorted, loaded with mids. That’s not a tone I’d reach for in most of my mixes. But the MOTÖRBASS surprised me by adding mids and highs in just the right proportions, so the bass still sounds like bass. It cuts through the guitars without turning to mush. That combination of aggression and clarity is harder to find than you’d think. Controls Three controls, clearly named. FASTER is gain, running from almost clean up to full blast. LOUDER is volume. HARDER shapes the upper mids: turned down it stays rounded and thick, turned up it adds aggressive bite and attack. Panel order from left to right: FASTER and LOUDER sit side by side as the two large knobs, with HARDER as a smaller knob tucked below center. In the demo above I’ve set up sweeps for both FASTER and HARDER so you can hear what each one does across its full range. How It Sounds “Tamed Beast” shows the pedal at restrained gain with a moderate HARDER setting, just enough grit to give the bass presence without shredding the signal. Crank FASTER and HARDER up for “Bare Teeth” and the upper mids bite hard while the low end holds firm underneath. “Full Roar” pushes gain and volume both to ten: grinding, full, and surprisingly usable in context. “Fat Punch” brings everything to noon as a balanced reference point. What I keep coming back to is how little I need to touch the EQ after recording with this pedal. The gain structure is gnarly but controlled, and the HARDER knob handles the tonal shaping in a way that lands without extra surgery in post. It also works as a light boost to push the front end of an amp. And yes, I’ve tested it on guitar: it stacks well and sounds great, though bass is clearly where it lives. MOTÖRBASS vs Basstortion The ZVEX Basstortion is the obvious cross-shop here: three controls, designed specifically for bass, and built around retaining low end under distortion. The Basstortion leans brighter and more open-sounding, especially in its Bright mode, which gives it a more guitar-like clang. The MOTÖRBASS is thicker and more mid-forward by default, sitting deeper in the mix rather than cutting across it. The Basstortion also has a DARK mode that smooths the top end out considerably, making it the more flexible option between the two if you need a wider range of characters. The MOTÖRBASS has a more focused identity: aggressive, punchy mid-driven rock distortion. Less range, but a stronger personality in that lane. Who It’s For Rock and hard rock bass players who want a distortion that adds mid-range presence without thinning out the low end. It’s well suited to shortscale basses, flatwounds, and pick playing, which is how I run it. If your ideal bass distortion is bright and cutting rather than thick and grindy, the MOTÖRBASS probably isn’t your pedal. If you want something that gets out of the way and makes every heavy backing track sound better without a second thought, it’s hard to argue with. Specs Circuit: bass distortion with internal 24V charge pump Power: 9V DC (standard center-negative); internal charge pump to 24V Controls: FASTER (gain), LOUDER (volume), HARDER (upper mid tone) Signal Chain JMJ Mustang Bass* with La Bella Flats* , Curtis Novak FAT Mustang Pickups, played with a pick MOTÖRBASS Strymon Iridium (round mode with OwnHammer AMPG Bass
